issues.legal_issue: A transferee under a pre-amendment transfer of resumed service-inam land acquires title when the land is subsequently re-granted to the transferor.
material_facts: The land was service-inam land held by the transferor and his father before the appointed date under the governing legislation.
The transferor and his father sold the land by registered sale deed in 1971, after the appointed date and before the 1978 amendment, and the transferee took possession.
The land was subsequently re-granted to the transferor, and the re-grant in his favour became final.
The transferee’s successor brought a civil suit seeking a declaration of ownership and an injunction.
issues.conclusion: The subsequent re-grant to the transferor enured to the benefit of the transferee, who acquired good title to the land upon re-grant.
issues.legal_principle: Under Sections 4, 5 and 6 of the Karnataka Village Offices Act, 1961, land resumed on abolition of village offices could be re-granted to the holder or authorised holder. The Karnataka High Court’s decisions in Lakshmana Gowda v. State of Karnataka and Syed Bhasheer Ahamed v. State of Karnataka establish that an alienation made after the Act came into force but before the 1978 amendment was not invalid merely because it preceded re-grant; title acquired on re-grant related back to the Act’s commencement. The doctrine of feeding the grant by estoppel under Section 43 of the Transfer of Property Act therefore allowed the later-acquired title to benefit the alienee.

predicates.civil_title_claim: A transferee or the transferee’s successor brought a civil proceeding claiming ownership of the land.
predicates.transfer_after_abolition_before_restrict: The holder transferred the land after abolition of the village office but before the later amendment restricting transfers took effect.
predicates.land_regranted_to_transferor: The land was subsequently re-granted to the person who had transferred it.

issues.definition: When a civil ownership claim concerns a transfer made after abolition but before the later restriction, and the land is re-granted to the transferor, the transferee acquires title upon re-grant.

issues.legal_issue: A transferee under a transfer made before the 1978 amendment is not an unauthorised holder subject to eviction under the statutory eviction procedure merely because the transfer preceded re-grant.
material_facts: The land was transferred in 1971, after the appointed date and before the 1978 amendment, and the transferee took possession.
The transferee was evicted in 1981 pursuant to proceedings initiated by the Tehsildar under Section 7 of the Act.
The land was later re-granted to the transferor, and that re-grant became final.
The High Court relied on the prior eviction to deny the transferee’s successor the benefit of the re-grant.
issues.conclusion: The Tehsildar was not competent to initiate eviction proceedings under Section 7 against the transferee, who was not an unauthorised holder; the prior eviction did not defeat the transferee’s claim.
issues.legal_principle: Section 7 of the Karnataka Village Offices Act, 1961, as amended, provides for eviction of unauthorised holders. Syed Bhasheer Ahamed v. State of Karnataka held that a transferee under an alienation made between the appointed date and the 1978 amendment is not an unauthorised holder and cannot be evicted under Section 7 on that basis. The Court applied that principle together with Lakshmana Gowda v. State of Karnataka and held that the alienee’s rights were not displaced by the eviction proceedings.

predicates.statutory_eviction_proceeding: An authority initiated a statutory proceeding to evict a person from land resumed after abolition of a village office.
predicates.transfer_after_abolition_before_restrict: The holder transferred the land after abolition of the village office but before the later amendment restricting transfers took effect.
predicates.transferee_possessed_land_under_transfer: The transferee possessed the land pursuant to the transfer.

issues.definition: An authority lacks competence to evict a transferee through the statutory procedure when the transferee possessed land under a transfer made after abolition but before the later restriction.
